QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_74

question.text: As the IM of an open-ended Cat III AIF, you are designing performance-fee crystallisation. Which approach is MOST consistent with the workbook's treatment of incentive-fee crystallisation and the High-Water Mark?

answer.text: Pay performance fee monthly with no HWM threshold
Pay performance fee weekly to maximise immediate manager incentive
Crystallise on a longer cycle (typically a 3-year cycle or at fund end) subject to the HWM, with daily accrual of performance fee in NAV
Pay performance fee only when the NAV is positive in a single month, regardless of HWM

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook treats HWM as the threshold that must be exceeded before incentive fees can be paid and discourages paying incentive fees before later losses are known. For Category III AIFs, the workbook indicates that performance fees are mostly calculated on a 3-year cycle or at fund end, with daily accrual into NAV in the meantime. The Trap: Options A and B pay too frequently and ignore the HWM. Option D rewards a single positive month without the HWM threshold. Note: Daily accrual ensures that subscriptions and redemptions transact at a NAV that already reflects accrued performance fee.
